title: Handbook: Investment companies
accounting_bases: US GAAP, including ASC 946; SEC presentation when applicable
source_classification: Professional-firm technical interpretation with reproduced Codification/AICPA excerpts and examples
questions: management fees, expense offsets and waivers
carry, incentive allocation and clawback presentation
inspected_summary: KPMG identifies ASC 946 scope characteristics and states that in-scope investment company investments are generally measured at fair value. It explains Topic 946 capital transaction timing: fund share orders are trade-date or effective-date events as applicable, while nonregistered investment partnerships record commitments on the date specified by governing documents and early cash as an advance-capital-contribution liability. Investor classes require NAV and share transaction reporting. It reproduces AICPA TQA 6910.29: for a nonregistered investment partnership reporting capital by class, cumulative unrealized gains/losses, carry and clawback are reflected as if assets were realized at reported fair value and liabilities settled, then allocated/distributed according to governing documents. Adviser charges may be fund expense, disproportionate income allocation to GP capital, or both; the agreement and relevant disclosures matter. Loss carryforwards reduce future performance fees but are not themselves an asset. Equalization accounting for investment-company shares tracks credits/debits included in issuance/repurchase prices as separately presented undistributed investment income.
locators: About this publication and August 2026 edition; §§1.1-1.2 / ASC 946 scope, pages 3-17; §§4.1-4.3 capital/NAV, pages 172-180; TQA 6910.29 carry/clawback, pages 180-182 and 220-225; §5.1 adviser transactions, pages 216-218; equalization, pages 452 and 457

title: The ILPA Model Limited Partnership Agreement (Deal-by-Deal Waterfall)
accounting_bases: contractual distribution/economic terms; federal partnership-tax clauses also illustrated
source_classification: Industry association model contract; illustrative negotiated terms, not accounting authority or law
questions: deal-by-deal waterfall tiers and preferred return/catch-up/carry
escrow, interim/final clawback and LP giveback
fund vs GP rights and allocations
inspected_summary: The public model LPA gives a bounded deal-by-deal sequence: distribute first to the LP until contributions used for the specific investment, other realized investments, aggregate unrealized losses, Fund Expenses and management fee are returned; second, 100% to the LP until a bracketed 8% annual preferred return, compounded annually and calculated daily from receipt of each qualifying contribution, is paid; third, a bracketed 80% GP/20% LP catch-up (or 100% to LP alternative) until GP carry equals a bracketed 20% of cumulative profits after contributed capital; then 20% GP/80% LP. It also contains interim/final GP clawback with an escrow option, LP giveback, and separate book/net income and tax allocation articles. Model terms, bracketed alternatives and tax provisions are not accounting authority or a universal market agreement.
locators: Official ILPA model page, July 1, 2020 date and Delaware-law scope; definition of Preferred Return, §1.1, PDF pages 12-14; §§14.3 waterfall, 14.7 clawback, 14.9-14.12 book and tax allocations, PDF pages 48-55
